sources.title: U.S. Small Business Administration, Close or sell your business
quotes: Use business valuation to set a monetary value.
[Income approach] Looks at projected revenue and accounts for potential risks.
[Market approach] Compares your business to other similar businesses that have recently sold.
[Assets approach] Subtracts total business liabilities from the total value of all assets.

Accurately value all property and real estate tied to your small business. This can include intangible assets like brand presence, intellectual property, customer information, and projection of future revenue.
facts: Recommends an attorney review the sales agreement.

sources.title: U.S. Small Business Administration, Buy an existing business or franchise
quotes: thorough, objective investigation
Consider hiring an attorney and an accountant.
facts: Lists financial statements and tax returns among documents to evaluate.
Says to ask about contracts, leases, existing cash flow and inventory.
Names a letter of intent, confidentiality agreement, sales agreement and purchase price adjustment as documents professionals can help with.

sources.title: Corporate Finance Institute, Multiples analysis
quotes: utilizes different financial metrics from comparable companies to value a target company
make quick computations to assess a company's value
It only considers the company's position for a certain time period
facts: Lists oversimplification and comparability problems (different accounting methods) as disadvantages.

sources.title: Corporate Finance Institute, Enterprise Value (EV)
quotes: Enterprise Value (EV) is the measure of a company's total value.
facts: EV = market capitalization + market value of debt - cash and equivalents.

sources.title: Corporate Finance Institute, Enterprise Value to Revenue Multiple
quotes: ignores profitability and cash flow generation
does not take into account the company's capital structure
facts: Used when a company has no positive EBITDA or net income.

sources.title: Corporate Finance Institute, Revenue Run Rate
quotes: takes a company's current revenue in a certain period (a week, month, quarter, etc.) and converts it to an annual figure
facts: Risks listed: assumes conditions stay unchanged, seasonality, one-off events.

sources.title: Corporate Finance Institute, DCF Formula
quotes: used to value investments by discounting the estimated future cash flows
facts: Discount rate is typically the weighted average cost of capital.

sources.title: Corporate Finance Institute, Trailing Twelve Months (TTM)
facts: TTM = latest fiscal year + current year to date - prior-year same period. Also called LTM.

sources.title: Stripe, Essential SaaS metrics
quotes: The total amount of money a company can expect to receive from its existing customers each month.
The percentage of total customers who discontinue using a product or service during a given period.
The percentage of revenue that is retained from existing customers over a given period of time.
facts: Defines MRR, ARR, churn and net revenue retention as quoted. Does not define the Rule of 40.

sources.title: BizBuySell Learning Center, Add-Backs for Seller's Discretionary Earnings
quotes: Add-backs are expenses added back to a company's bottom-line profits when determining Seller's Discretionary Earnings (SDE) or EBITDA.
some add-backs can unrealistically overvalue the company
facts: Categories: discretionary personal, discretionary operating, non-operating, non-recurring, depreciation and amortization.

sources.title: Internal Revenue Service, Publication 561
quotes: FMV is the price that property would sell for on the open market.
